c.tagline: Ancient walls, Caspian shores, and a flame-lit skyline.

taxi.fareNote: Official Baku Taxi cabs are metered and red; agree fare upfront or use Bolt/Uber for transparent pricing, especially from the airport.

emergency.note: General emergency line 112 also connects to police, fire, and ambulance services.

avoid.reason: Safe; do not travel to Nagorno-Karabakh or front-line border areas

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed walled Old City (Icherisheher) with cobblestone lanes, the Maiden Tower and Shirvanshahs' Palace; ideal for first-time visitors who want history and atmosphere within walking distance of everything.
Baku's lively pedestrian core around Fountains Square and Nizami Street, packed with cafes, shopping and nightlife; suits visitors who want a central base near restaurants and metro access.
The palm-lined Caspian seafront Boulevard beneath the Flame Towers in Sabayil, home to upscale hotels, parks and Crystal Hall; best for travelers wanting sea views and easy access to landmark sights.
A buzzing entertainment and dining district packed with restaurants, bars and clubs; suited to visitors who want to be close to Baku's nightlife scene.
A residential, mostly local neighborhood away from the tourist core with everyday markets, cheaper stays and easy metro links; good for budget travelers wanting an authentic, non-touristy base.

water.note: Despite treatment upgrades, most residents and all visitors are advised to use bottled or filtered water.

transit.pay: Visitors buy a rechargeable BakuKart smart card (small refundable deposit) at metro stations or kiosks, which works across metro, bus, funicular and Aeroexpress airport bus. Cards can be topped up with cash or card at station machines and validated by tapping on entry.
transit.hours: Metro operates roughly 6:00-24:00; BakuBus network runs similar hours with some 24-hour routes like the airport H1 line.
transit.note: Metro has 3 lines (Red, Green, Purple) with about 27 stations; extensive city bus network covers areas metro doesn't reach.

train: Baku Railway Station (domestic and international routes including Tbilisi and the Baku-Tbilisi-Kars line)
bus: Intercity buses from Baku International Bus Terminal
ferry: Baku International Sea Trade Port (Caspian Sea ferries to Aktau, Kazakhstan and Turkmenbashi, Turkmenistan)

transit.m: Aeroexpress bus to 28 May metro station (~30 min, every 20-60 min, 06:00-23:15)
BakuBus H1 24-hour line to city center

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants is appreciated, especially where service isn't included.

food.name: Shah plov
food.desc: Azerbaijan's crowned rice dish: saffron pilaf with lamb, dried fruit and nuts, baked in a golden lavash crust and carved open at the table.

places.name: Plov House
places.note: Specialist famous for many varieties of plov

places.name: Sehrli Tendir
places.area: Old City, by the Maiden Tower
places.note: Clay-oven cooking; its tandir bread and plov come highly recommended

food.name: Dolma
food.desc: Grape leaves or baby vegetables stuffed with minced lamb, rice and herbs, served with garlic yogurt - Azerbaijani home cooking at its best.

places.name: Dolma Restaurant
places.note: Named for the dish; a reliable classic for grape-leaf dolma

places.name: Qaynana (Gaynana)
places.note: 'Mother-in-law' homestyle spot whose dolma tastes homemade, per recent reviews

food.name: Qutab
food.desc: Paper-thin half-moon flatbreads griddled on a saj and stuffed with herbs, cheese, meat or pumpkin - Baku's favorite quick bite.

places.name: Firuze
places.note: Long-running national-cuisine cellar known for classic qutab and kebabs

places.name: Qaynana (Gaynana)
places.note: Herb and meat qutab off the griddle in a rustic courtyard setting

food.name: Lyulya kebab
food.desc: Minced lamb kebabs grilled over open flame, wrapped in fluffy lavash with sumac onions - the smoky heart of Azerbaijani dining.

places.name: Mangal
places.note: Open-fire grill, fluffy lavash and generous portions per recent guides

places.name: Shirvanshah Museum Restaurant
places.note: Museum-like halls, live mugham music and classic kebab platters

food.name: Caspian fish levengi
food.desc: Caspian fish stuffed with a tangy walnut, onion and sour plum paste, then baked - a southern Azerbaijani specialty worth seeking out.

places.name: Sumakh
places.note: Upscale Azerbaijani dining room praised for refined regional classics

places.name: Chayki
places.note: Chic Caspian-view spot with impeccable fish, per recent reviews

food.name: Armudu black tea
food.desc: Strong black tea in pear-shaped armudu glasses, sipped through a sugar cube with fruit preserves - Azerbaijan's hospitality ritual.

places.name: Cay Bagi 145 (Tea Garden 145)
places.note: Tea on a hammam rooftop with Caspian views; 4.8-rated on Tripadvisor

places.name: Armudu Lounge and Tea House
places.note: Open since 2007; samovar tea with jams and sweets

food.name: Pomegranate wine
food.desc: Azerbaijan turns its national fruit into a ruby-red wine - try it by the glass alongside local grape varieties like Madrasa.

places.name: Kefli Local Wine and Snacks
places.note: The city's best-known spot for Azerbaijani wines, including pomegranate wine

places.name: Sumakh
places.note: Deep local wine list to pair with upscale national dishes

landmarks: Flame Towers
These three shimmering skyscrapers dominate Baku's skyline, changing color at night to mimic flickering flames in tribute to the nation's fiery Zoroastrian heritage.
Heydar Aliyev Center
Zaha Hadid's flowing, wave-like white building has no straight lines or right angles, making it one of the world's most photographed pieces of contemporary architecture.
Maiden Tower (Qız Qalası)
This mysterious 12th-century stone tower in the Old City is a UNESCO-listed symbol of Baku, its true original purpose still debated by historians.
Palace of the Shirvanshahs
This 15th-century royal residence within the walled Old City showcases exquisite medieval Islamic architecture and was once home to Azerbaijan's ruling dynasty.
Icherisheher (Old City)
Baku's ancient walled quarter of winding cobblestone lanes, caravanserais, and centuries-old mosques offers an atmospheric contrast to the city's futuristic skyline.
Baku Boulevard
This lively seaside promenade along the Caspian Sea stretches for miles, lined with parks, cafes, and views of the city's dramatic modern skyline.
Fountains Square
The bustling heart of downtown Baku, this pedestrian plaza is filled with sculpted fountains, cafes, and shops, buzzing with locals and tourists alike.
Martyrs' Lane
This hillside memorial and eternal flame honor those who died for Azerbaijan's independence, also offering one of the best panoramic viewpoints over the city and bay.
Baku Ferris Wheel (Baku Eye)
This giant illuminated wheel on the boulevard offers sweeping views over the Caspian coastline and is a favorite spot for evening photographs of the glowing skyline.
Nizami Street
Baku's grand pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century facades, shops and cafes, running from Fountains Square past the opera house through the heart of downtown.

train.note: Trains leave from Baku Railway Station (28 May). The overnight Baku-Tbilisi sleeper resumed in 2025 after a six-year gap; bring your passport for the border check en route.

bus.note: All international coaches depart the Baku International Bus Terminal near the airport (Bina). Buy tickets at the terminal counters; passport and destination visa required.

ferry.note: Caspian ferries leave from Alat port about 70 km south of Baku, not the city itself. These are cargo/Ro-Ro ships that also take passengers, with no fixed timetable - be ready to wait. Arrange Turkmenistan/Kazakhstan visas in advance.

half.name: Gobustan National Park
half.blurb: Ancient rock carvings and bubbling mud volcanoes scattered across a stark, otherworldly desert landscape.

half.name: Yanar Dag
half.blurb: Natural gas fire that has blazed continuously on a hillside for many centuries.

half.name: Ateshgah Fire Temple
half.blurb: Historic pentagonal fire temple where flames once drew Zoroastrian and Hindu pilgrims.

full.name: Quba
full.blurb: Charming Caucasus-foothill town known for orchards, carpets and the historic Red Village.

full.name: Lahic
full.blurb: Cobblestoned mountain village celebrated for its coppersmiths and traditional Caucasus craftsmanship.

full.name: Gabala
full.blurb: Green mountain resort region with forests, waterfalls and views of the Greater Caucasus.
